mainTopic: How much of קריאת שמע needs כוונה, the special status of the first פסוק, body position while saying שמע, and greeting people during it
overview: This amud asks how much of קריאת שמע needs כוונה. רבי יוחנן rules that the first paragraph needs it, in two versions that agree in practice. רב זוטרא and רבי יאשיה argue about which paragraph needs כוונה and which needs reading, and the גמרא defends each view against challenges from the פסוקים. רבא rules like רבי מאיר, who says only the first פסוק needs כוונה. The גמרא then teaches how to draw out the word אחד, and argues about how much of שמע must be said standing in place. Stories about רבי, רב נחמן and רבה show that the first פסוק alone fulfills the basic obligation. Next comes the rule against saying שמע while lying on one's back. The amud ends by explaining the משנה's rules for greeting people during שמע, where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's proof that the whole section needs intent
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי עקיבא's proof from the פסוק: because the words 'upon your heart' sit inside a description of the whole section, the whole פרשה needs כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Which I command you today, upon your heart." From here you learn that the whole section, all of it, needs focused intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי עקיבא's proof from the פסוק. He concludes that the entire first פרשה of שמע needs כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'upon your heart' is attached to 'these words which I command you today', and those words refer to the whole section. So the 'heart' requirement covers all of it. This argues against the view that only the opening part needs כוונה.

steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from the word 'והיו' that שמע must not be read out of order.

steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיו' means 'they shall be', so the words must stay as they are written. Reading them in a different order would break that. This is a new requirement about order, separate from כוונה.

steps.title: רב זוטרא and רבי יאשיה disagree about intent and reading
steps.stepSummary: On the words 'על לבבך', רב זוטרא says the part before needs כוונה and the part after needs only reading. רבי יאשיה says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Upon your heart': רב זוטרא says up to here is the מצוה of כוונה, and from here on is the מצוה of reading. רבי יאשיה says up to here is the מצוה of reading, and from here on is the מצוה of כוונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא records a מחלוקת about where the words 'על לבבך' draw the line between the part that needs כוונה and the part that needs reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both learn from 'על לבבך' that שמע has two zones: the first paragraph, and what comes after it. They disagree about which zone gets which מצוה. רב זוטרא puts כוונה in the first paragraph, and רבי יאשיה puts it after.

steps.title: Why Only Reading After 'On Your Heart'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב זוטרא: if the second section needs reading because it says 'to speak of them,' the first section also says 'and you shall speak of them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the part from here on, that it has a מצוה of reading? Is it because it is written 'to speak of them'? But here too, in the first section, it is written 'and you shall speak of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב זוטרא. It first reads him as saying the first section needs only כוונה and the later part needs only reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later part has a מצוה of reading because the פסוק says 'לדבר בם' (to speak of them). But the first section also says 'ודברת בם' (and you shall speak of them). So reading should be required in the first section too, and the split seems not to work.

steps.title: That Verse Teaches About Placing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The 'heart' words in the second section are used for a different law, from רבי יצחק: the arm תפילין must be placed opposite the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one is needed for the teaching of רבי יצחק, who said: 'And you shall place these words of Mine' teaches that the placing must be opposite the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'heart' wording in the second section teaches something else, so it cannot teach כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second section, 'ושמתם את דברי אלה על לבבכם' is about physically placing the words, meaning the תפילין, by the heart. רבי יצחק learns from it that the arm תפילין go opposite the heart. Since this פסוק is already used for that law, only the first section teaches כוונה, and רב זוטרא's split stands.

steps.title: Why should only the second paragraph need intent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יאשיה (reading up to here, intent from here on) and challenges him: the first paragraph also says 'on your heart.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יאשיה says, up to here is the מצוה of reading, and from here on is the מצוה of intent. What makes the later part special for intent? Because it says 'on your heart' (עַל לְבַבְכֶם)? But here, in the first part, it also says 'on your heart' (עַל לְבָבֶךָ)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יאשיה's opinion from the ברייתא and attacks it. It asks why the second paragraph alone should need כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה seems to learn כוונה from the words 'on your heart' in the second paragraph. But the first paragraph has those same words. So the first paragraph should need כוונה too, and his split seems to fall apart. This is the mirror image of the challenge against רב זוטרא in step 9.

steps.title: 'To speak of them' in the second paragraph is about teaching Torah
steps.stepSummary: The 'to speak of them' in the second paragraph refers to teaching children Torah, not to reciting שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about Torah study. This is what the Torah is saying: teach your children Torah, so that they will be well-versed in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second paragraph's 'to speak of them' is about something else entirely. It is a command to teach Torah to your children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second paragraph, 'to speak of them' is part of 'and you shall teach them to your children.' So it describes the goal of teaching children Torah until they are fluent in it, and it is not a rule for reciting קריאת שמע. This leaves the second paragraph with כוונה but no קריאה requirement, as רבי יאשיה said. It parallels step 10, where 'on your heart' was also used for a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of Torah; Torah study in general
'The Merciful One', a name for G-d as the giver of the Torah
Teach (plural command)
They will study fluently and be well-versed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יאשיה, the first paragraph of שמע needs both קריאה and כוונה. The second needs only כוונה, because its 'to speak of them' is about teaching children Torah.

phrases.english: That verse is written about Torah study.
And this is what the Merciful One says:
Teach your children Torah,
so that they will be well-versed in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 13 by giving the verse a different purpose
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is applied to a different topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'To speak of them' in the second paragraph requires reading קריאת שמע
steps.terutzMaskana: It commands teaching children Torah so they become fluent, so the second paragraph has no reading requirement

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Only the first verse needs focused intent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: כוונת הלב is needed only up to the end of the first פסוק of שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One". Up to here, focused intent of the heart is required. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא giving one more opinion on how much of שמע needs focused intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions stretched the intent requirement over a whole paragraph or more. רבי מאיר limits it to the single פסוק of שמע ישראל, the verse where we accept God as One. After that verse, saying the words is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent of the heart, meaning focused attention on what you are saying
Up to here

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: up to here, intent of the heart is required,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over רבי יאשיה's view, this adds another opinion: intent is needed only for the first פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כוונת הלב is required only for the פסוק שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא decides that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical ruling: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר's view from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several opinions were raised about how much of שמע needs intent. רבא settles it in practice: you must have intent for the first פסוק only.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, focused intent is required only for the first פסוק of שמע, following רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for how we say קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the opinion quoted in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר: intent is needed only for the first פסוק.

steps.title: סומכוס: Drawing out the word אחד brings long life
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס teaches that a person who draws out the word אחד is rewarded with a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: סומכוס says: Whoever draws out the word "One" will have his days and years drawn out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how to say the word אחד in the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking extra time on אחד gives a person room to think about God being One. The reward matches the act: he lengthens the word, so his life is lengthened.

keyTerms.meaning: One who draws out or lengthens
"One", the last word of the פסוק שמע ישראל

phrases.english: It was taught: Sumchos says:
Whoever draws out the word "One,"
they draw out for him his days and his years.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the first פסוק and moves from intent to how the last word is said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing out the word אחד earns a long life.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: Draw out the ד
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב adds that the lengthening should be on the last letter, the ד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: And on the ד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב explains which part of the word אחד should be drawn out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס said to lengthen אחד but did not say where. רב אחא בר יעקב says to stretch the final ד, so the word comes out complete and clear.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ד, the last letter of אחד

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
And on the dalet.
phrases.notes: He means the stretching should happen on the final letter ד of אחד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וּבַדָּלֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how to carry out סומכוס's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lengthening of אחד goes on the letter ד.

steps.title: רב אשי: Don't rush the ח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי warns that while drawing out the ד, one must not swallow or rush the ח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: As long as he does not rush through the ח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit so that stretching the ד doesn't harm the rest of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone focused on the ד might hurry through the ח before it. רב אשי says the whole word must still be said properly, ח included.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as, provided that
Will snatch, meaning say too quickly
The letter ח, the middle letter of אחד

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
As long as he does not rush through the chet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲטוֹף בַּחֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the lengthening described in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When lengthening the ד, the ח must not be rushed.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: You don't need to stretch it too long
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה saw רבי חייא בר אבא drawing out אחד a great deal. He told him that once he has crowned God over everything, he does not need to go on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting before רבי חייא בר אבא and saw him drawing out the word a great deal. He said to him: Once you have crowned Him above, below, and in all four directions of the heavens, you don't need any more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets an upper limit on how long to draw out אחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the lengthening is to think about God ruling over everything: up, down, and in every direction. Once those thoughts are complete, stretching the word further adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him
A lot, very much
You have made Him King, crowned Him
You don't need any more

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmiyah was sitting
before Rabbi Chiya bar Abba,
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets comes from the corrected wording. Some versions have a different name here.

phrases.english: he saw that he was drawing out the word a great deal,
he said to him:
Once you have crowned Him
above and below
and in the four directions of the heavens,
you don't need any more.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the maximum length for the lengthening that סומכוס praised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Draw out אחד only long enough to think of God ruling in all directions, and no longer.
steps.whatToRemember: Draw out אחד, mainly on the ד, without rushing the ח. Take only as long as it takes to think of God ruling everywhere.

steps.title: רב יהודה: "On your heart" while standing
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר מר עוקבא quotes רב יהודה: the words "על לבבך" must be said while standing in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר מר עוקבא said in the name of רב יהודה: "On your heart", while standing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: which part of שמע must be said while standing still. The גמרא will question this wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה links standing still to the phrase "על לבבך" from the first paragraph. As written, it sounds like only those two words need standing, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: "On your heart", from the first paragraph of שמע
While standing, meaning staying in one place rather than walking

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר מָר עוּקְבָא
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Mar Ukva said
that Rav Yehuda said:
"On your heart" while standing.
phrases.notes: דברים 6:6. Standing here means stopping in one place instead of walking, not getting up from a seat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of intent and lengthening to standing in place while saying שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Part of שמע, connected to "על לבבך", must be said while standing in place.
steps.confusionAlert: Standing here does not mean getting up from a chair. It means not walking, staying in one place.

steps.title: Can it really mean just those two words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how standing could be required only for the words "על לבבך".
steps.simpleTranslation: "On your heart"? Could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יהודה's statement as it was quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing special about the two words "על לבבך" would make only them need standing. So the statement cannot be read literally, and the next step will fix the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A way of saying an idea makes no sense.

phrases.english: "On your heart"? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל לְבָבֶךָ״ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense to require standing for only two words out of the middle of a paragraph.

steps.title: Corrected reading: Stand until "on your heart"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the statement: everything up to "על לבבך" must be said standing, and after that, standing is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: up to "on your heart", while standing. From here on, not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב יהודה's statement so it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "על לבבך" marks a stopping point, not the only words that need standing. Everything from the start of שמע until those words must be said standing in place. The rest may be said while walking.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. It introduces a corrected reading.
From here onward

phrases.english: Rather, say:
up to "on your heart" while standing.
From here on, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by changing how the statement is read.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the words "על לבבך" need standing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything up to and including "על לבבך" needs standing; after that, it does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The whole paragraph while standing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the entire first paragraph must be said while standing in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The entire paragraph, all of it, while standing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second, stricter opinion on how much of שמע needs standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה requires standing only until "על לבבך". רבי יוחנן extends it to the whole first paragraph. So the dispute is over the part of the paragraph after "על לבבך".

keyTerms.meaning: A paragraph or section of the Torah. Here it means the first paragraph of שמע.
All of it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The entire paragraph, all of it, while standing.
phrases.notes: He means the first paragraph of שמע, which ends with "ובשעריך".

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ בַּעֲמִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's corrected view from step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole first paragraph of שמע must be said while standing in place.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה: stand until "על לבבך". רבי יוחנן: stand for the whole first paragraph.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent with his ruling elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן's view, that the whole first paragraph must be said standing, fits his ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is following his own reasoning. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי אחא, who spoke in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's statement in the last step is not new. It matches another ruling he gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on this דף, רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה held that the whole first paragraph is special and needs כוונה. רבי יוחנן rules like him there. So it makes sense that he also requires standing for the whole first paragraph.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning. In other words, he is consistent with what he said elsewhere.
The practical law follows this opinion
In the name of

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Acha
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אחא's earlier view on the דף: the whole first paragraph needs כוונה.

phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's view from step 24 by showing he is consistent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה, which fits his view that the whole first paragraph is special and must be said standing.

steps.title: רבי's שמע was just the first verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the single פסוק שמע ישראל was the whole קריאת שמע of רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Hear Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' This was רבי יהודה הנשיא's קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It tells us that רבי יהודה הנשיא said only the first פסוק as his קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The first פסוק is the core of accepting מלכות שמים, and רבי relied on it alone. The next steps ask how and when he did this.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of שמע

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: this is the reading of Shema
of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about how much of שמע a person must say.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה הנשיא fulfilled קריאת שמע with the first פסוק alone.

steps.title: רב never saw רבי accept the kingship of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רבי חייא that he never saw רבי say שמע at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: I never saw רבי accept upon himself the kingship of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב is puzzled. He was around רבי but never saw him say שמע, not even the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a one-פסוק שמע should be visible to a student. רב's comment is really a question: when did רבי do it? This sets up רבי חייא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship of Heaven. Saying שמע is accepting it.
I did not see

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Chiyya:
I did not see Rebbi
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: accept upon himself the kingship of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא: לָא חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions when רבי actually said his one-פסוק שמע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When and how did רבי accept מלכות שמים, if רב never saw it?

steps.title: רבי said it while passing his hands over his face
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that when רבי covered his face with his hands, he was accepting עול מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Son of nobles, when he passes his hands over his face, he is accepting upon himself the yoke of the kingship of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רב. רבי did say שמע, but quietly, in the middle of teaching, while passing his hands over his face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That is why רב missed it. The short gesture was the moment רבי said the first פסוק. This fits the ברייתא that his שמע was one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of nobles. A respectful way of addressing רב.
Passes his hands over his face
The yoke of the kingship of Heaven

phrases.english: He said to him: Son of nobles,
phrases.notes: רבי חייא is answering here. He was רב's uncle.

phrases.english: at the time he passes his hands over his face,
he accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingship of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּר פַּחֲתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's puzzlement from step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי said the first פסוק at the moment he passed his hands over his face, so it was easy to miss.

steps.title: Did רבי finish שמע later?
steps.stepSummary: The question is raised whether רבי went back later to say the rest of שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he go back and finish it, or does he not go back and finish it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question. Was the one פסוק all he said, or did he finish שמע later?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 26 and 28 showed that רבי said one פסוק in the middle of learning. Now the question is whether that was his whole מצוה or just the key part. Two opinions follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and finishes it

phrases.english: Does he go back and finish it,
or does he not go back and finish it?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וְגוֹמְרָהּ, אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וְגוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about רבי's practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי say the rest of שמע later, after his one-פסוק acceptance?

steps.title: בר קפרא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא says רבי did not finish שמע later. רבי שמעון ברבי says he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא says: He does not go back and finish it. רבי שמעון the son of רבי says: He goes back and finishes it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two people who knew רבי give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בר קפרא, the one פסוק was רבי's whole קריאת שמע. For רבי שמעון ברבי, it was only a quick acceptance in its time, and the full שמע came later.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of רבי

phrases.english: Bar Kappara says:
He does not go back and finish it.
Rabbi Shimon, son of Rebbi, says:
He goes back and finishes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר קַפָּרָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בר קפרא: he did not finish later. רבי שמעון ברבי: he finished later.

steps.title: Why would רבי look for a topic about leaving Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא challenges רבי שמעון. If רבי finished שמע later, why did he go out of his way to teach a topic that mentions יציאת מצרים?
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to רבי שמעון ברבי: It makes sense by me, since I say he does not go back and finish it. That is why רבי looks for a teaching that has יציאת מצרים in it. But according to you, who says he goes back and finishes it, why does he need to look for one?
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא uses something everyone saw רבי do to attack רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי would make a point of teaching a topic that mentions יציאת מצרים. For בר קפרא this is easy: since רבי never said the last paragraph of שמע, he needed another way to mention leaving Egypt. But if רבי said all of שמע later, the last paragraph would cover it, so why bother?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense according to me
Looks for, seeks out
Leaving Egypt. There is a מצוה to mention it.
A teaching, a topic of learning

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to Rabbi Shimon, son of Rebbi:
It makes sense according to me,
since I say "he does not go back and finish it,"
that is why Rebbi seeks out a teaching
that has the exodus from Egypt in it.
phrases.notes: Most people mention leaving Egypt in the last paragraph of שמע. בר קפרא holds רבי never said it.

phrases.english: But according to you, who says he goes back and finishes it,
why does he need to seek it out?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון ברבי's side of the dispute in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון ברבי's view that רבי finished שמע later
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי said the full שמע later, its last paragraph already mentions יציאת מצרים, so seeking out such a topic while teaching would be pointless.

steps.title: To mention leaving Egypt at the right time
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי wanted to mention יציאת מצרים during the proper time for קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In order to mention יציאת מצרים at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer defends רבי שמעון ברבי. Even if רבי finished שמע later, he still wanted to mention leaving Egypt on time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later full שמע might come after the proper time had passed. So רבי made sure to mention יציאת מצרים during the right time, just as he accepted מלכות שמים on time with the first פסוק. This shows that seeking out the topic is not proof for בר קפרא.

keyTerms.meaning: To mention
At its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: רבי said the first פסוק of שמע on time, in the middle of teaching. Whether he finished שמע later is disputed. Either way, he made sure to mention יציאת מצרים at the proper time.

phrases.english: In order to mention the exodus from Egypt at its proper time.
phrases.notes: 'Its time' means the time for saying שמע. The full שמע later might come after that.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי לְהַזְכִּיר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בִּזְמַנָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בר קפרא's challenge in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeking out a topic about יציאת מצרים only makes sense if רבי never said the last paragraph.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if he finished שמע later, he wanted to mention יציאת מצרים during its proper time.

steps.title: Saying the first פסוק and then falling asleep is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא, quoting רב, rules that one who said 'שמע ישראל' and was then overcome by sleep has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא son of רב שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: If someone said 'Hear, Israel, ה' is our God, ה' is One' and was then overcome by sleep, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that follows from the story of רבי: the first פסוק alone is enough to fulfill the basic obligation of קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that רבי said only the first פסוק at the proper time. Now רב makes it a clear rule. If sleep overtakes you after the first פסוק, you have fulfilled your obligation even though you did not finish.

keyTerms.meaning: Was overcome by sleep against his will
He fulfilled his obligation
In the name of רב

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the first פסוק is the essential core of קריאת שמע.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא בְּרֵיהּ דְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila, son of Rav Shmuel bar Marta, said
in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״
phrases.english: One who said 'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: and was overcome by sleep has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא בְּרֵיהּ דְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story of רבי saying only the first פסוק into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying the first פסוק of שמע fulfills the obligation, even if one then falls asleep.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks his servant to wake him only for the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells his servant דרו to make him stay awake for the first פסוק and not to bother him for more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to his servant דרו: For the first פסוק, bother me so I stay awake. For more than that, don't bother me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that supports רב's ruling. רב נחמן made sure to stay awake only for the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first פסוק were not enough, רב נחמן would have asked to be kept awake for the whole שמע. His practice shows he relied on the first פסוק alone when he was very tired.

keyTerms.meaning: Bother me (keep me from falling asleep)
The first פסוק
More than that

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Daru, his servant:
For the first verse, bother me;
phrases.notes: He means: if I am dozing off, shake me awake so I can say it.

phrases.english: for more than that, don't bother me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling with a practical story.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the first פסוק alone is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's instructions to his servant

steps.title: רבה also pushed himself only for the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רבה's son how his father behaved. He answers that רבה pushed himself to stay awake for the first פסוק only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked רב יוסף son of רבה: How did your father act? He answered: For the first פסוק he would push himself to stay awake. For more than that he would not push himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story supports the same rule. The great אמורא רבה also exerted himself only for the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question and answer form one short report about רבה's practice. It confirms that a second great teacher relied on the first פסוק alone, which strengthens רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Would push himself (to stay awake)
How did he act?

steps.whatToRemember: The basic obligation of קריאת שמע is fulfilled with the first פסוק. רבי, רב נחמן and רבה all relied on this.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to Rav Yosef, son of Rabba:
What would your father do?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּפְסוּקָא קַמָּא הֲוָה קָא מְצַעַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: For the first verse he would push himself;
phrases.notes: He means: push himself not to fall asleep.

phrases.english: for more than that he would not push himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting story to רב נחמן's.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the first פסוק alone is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבה as reported by his son

steps.title: One lying on his back may not say שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a person lying flat on his back may not say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A person lying on his back should not say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about body position during קריאת שמע. It starts with a ruling from רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying flat on one's back is an undignified position. רב יוסף says it is not a proper way to accept עול מלכות שמים through שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: One lying flat on his back
He should not recite

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: One lying on his back
may not recite Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף פְּרַקְדָּן לֹא יִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of sleep to the topic of position while saying שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not say קריאת שמע while lying on his back.

steps.title: Is sleeping on your back allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב יוסף implies sleeping on one's back is fine, when רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed anyone who sleeps that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only saying שמע that is forbidden in that position, so sleeping that way is fine? But רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed whoever sleeps on his back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges what seems to follow from רב יוסף's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only forbade saying שמע on one's back, which suggests that simply lying that way is acceptable. But רבי יהושע בן לוי treats sleeping on one's back as so bad that he cursed those who do it.

keyTerms.meaning: To lie down / sleep
It is fine, permitted
Curses
On one's back

phrases.english: Is it only reciting that he may not do,
but to lie down that way is fine?
But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
cursed one who sleeps on his back!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְרָא הוּא דְּלָא לִיקְרֵי הָא מִיגְנָא שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an implication of רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רב יוסף's ruling that lying on one's back is otherwise permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed those who sleep on their backs, so it cannot be permitted.

steps.title: Tilted to the side: sleeping is fine, saying שמע is not
steps.stepSummary: Sleeping on one's back while tilted slightly to the side is permitted, but saying שמע even in that tilted position is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: Sleeping that way while tilted slightly to the side is fine. But saying שמע is forbidden even when tilted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a middle position, lying on one's back but tilted a bit to the side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's curse is about sleeping completely flat. רב יוסף's case is the tilted position. Sleeping that way is allowed, but saying שמע needs more dignity, so it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Tilts to the side
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַצְלֵי does not mean 'prays'. It means leaning or tilting slightly to the side.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי, מִיגְנָא כִּי מַצְלֵי — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: They said: To lie down while tilted to the side is fine;

phrases.aramaic: מִקְרָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַצְלֵי נָמֵי — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but to recite, even though he is tilted, is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי מִיגְנָא כִּי מַצְלֵי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: רב יוסף is talking about lying on one's back while tilted to the side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב יוסף was talking about lying fully flat, so his words seemed to permit sleeping that way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fully flat is forbidden even for sleep. Tilted is fine for sleep but still forbidden for saying שמע.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said שמע while tilted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer, since רבי יוחנן used to lie tilted on his back and say שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן would lie tilted to the side and recite שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to רבי יוחנן's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer said saying שמע tilted is forbidden. But רבי יוחנן did exactly that, which suggests it is allowed. The answer to this challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Recites

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yoḥanan would tilt to the side and recite!
phrases.notes: He means: lying on his back, tilted a bit, while saying שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַצְלֵי וְקָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that saying שמע while tilted is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself said שמע while lying tilted, so it should be permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was a special case because he was heavy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's habit of saying שמע while lying tilted is not a proof, because he was heavy and could not easily read any other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is different, because he was a heavy man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 39. רבי יוחנן's practice does not prove that everyone may say שמע while tilted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 38 stays in place: saying שמע while tilted on the back is forbidden. רבי יוחנן was allowed only because of his body size, so his case is a personal exception, not a new general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: is different
a heavy, large-bodied person

steps.whatToRemember: Saying שמע while lying on one's back, even tilted, is forbidden. רבי יוחנן was an exception because he was heavy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan is different
because he was a heavy man.
phrases.notes: Literally 'a master of flesh.' He was so heavy that lying any other way was hard for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 39
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal exception: the case is different because of special circumstances
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's practice shows anyone may say שמע while tilted on the back
steps.terutzMaskana: His practice was a personal exception because he was heavy. The general rule forbidding it stands.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about greeting at the breaks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה about greeting people during קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the משנה and quotes its first words. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה is רבי מאיר's: at the breaks you may greet out of respect and respond, and in the middle you may greet out of fear and respond. The גמרא will now ask what the word 'and respond' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: the breaks between the paragraphs of שמע
greets someone first
'and so on': the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest is רבי מאיר's line from the משנה: greet out of respect and respond; in the middle, greet out of fear and respond.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּפְּרָקִים שׁוֹאֵל וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: at the breaks one greets out of respect and responds; in the middle one greets out of fear and responds.

steps.title: Responding for what reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one may respond at the breaks. If it is out of respect, that is obvious, since one may even greet first out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Responding, for what reason? If you say out of respect, then since one may even greet first, do we need to be told that one may respond?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'responds' means in the first clause, and shows why the simple reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting a greeting is a bigger interruption than answering one. If the משנה already allows greeting first out of respect, then answering out of respect is obvious. So 'responds' must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: responds to someone's greeting
for what reason?
if you say
now that... is it even needed? (if the bigger thing is allowed, the smaller is obvious)

phrases.english: He responds, for what reason?
If you say out of respect,
now that he may even greet first,
is it necessary to say he may respond?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵשִׁיב מֵחֲמַת מַאי? אִילֵּימָא מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the word 'responds' covers in the first clause

steps.title: One may answer anyone's greeting at the breaks
steps.stepSummary: At the breaks one greets out of respect, and one answers a greeting from any person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: he greets out of respect, and he answers a greeting from any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of the first clause. 'Responds' means you may answer anyone at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering is easier than greeting first, so the standard is lower. You greet first only someone who deserves respect, but you may answer even an ordinary person.

keyTerms.meaning: out of respect (for an important person)
to any person

phrases.english: Rather: he greets out of respect,
and he returns a greeting to any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד, וּמֵשִׁיב שָׁלוֹם לְכָל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 42
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At the breaks, one may answer a greeting from anyone, not only from someone who deserves respect.

steps.title: Now look at the second clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the second clause, about the middle of a paragraph, to test the same reading there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the later clause: 'And in the middle, he greets out of fear, and responds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It quotes the second clause, which also says 'and responds.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'responds' in the first clause adds a lower standard, the same word in the second clause must also add something. The next step checks what that could be.

keyTerms.meaning: say the later clause
in the middle of a paragraph
out of fear (of someone who could hurt you)

phrases.english: Say the later clause:
'And in the middle, he greets out of fear, and responds.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 43 against the second clause
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'responds' given in step 43
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears in the second clause and needs a parallel meaning, which will cause trouble.

steps.title: Responding in the middle, for what reason?
steps.stepSummary: If responding in the middle is out of fear, that is obvious, since one may even greet first out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Responding, for what reason? If you say out of fear, then since one may even greet first, do we need to be told that one may respond?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about the first clause, this time about the middle of a paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is the same as in step 42. If greeting first out of fear is allowed, answering out of fear is obvious, so 'responds' must mean something more.

keyTerms.meaning: to respond, to return a greeting

phrases.english: He responds, for what reason?
If you say out of fear,
now that he may even greet first,
is it necessary to say he may respond?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵשִׁיב מֵחֲמַת מַאי? אִילֵּימָא מִפְּנֵי הַיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the question of step 42 to the clause quoted in step 44
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the word 'responds' covers in the middle of a paragraph

steps.title: In the middle, one answers out of respect
steps.stepSummary: In the middle of a paragraph, one may answer a greeting even from someone who only deserves respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he responds out of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in the middle, 'responds' means you may answer even someone you are only showing respect to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greeting first in the middle needs the stronger reason of fear. Answering in the middle is allowed with the weaker reason of respect.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (gives the corrected explanation)

phrases.english: Rather, he responds out of respect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 45
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the middle, one may answer a greeting out of respect, even though greeting first needs fear.

steps.title: Now רבי מאיר sounds just like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: With these readings, רבי מאיר's view matches רבי יהודה's view in the משנה word for word. So what are they arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as רבי יהודה! For we learned: רבי יהודה says, in the middle he greets out of fear and responds out of respect, and at the breaks he greets out of respect and responds to anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. After the explanations in steps 43 and 46, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה seem to say exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה presents רבי יהודה as disagreeing with רבי מאיר. If the two views are now identical, there is no argument left, so the readings of רבי מאיר must be wrong somewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: that is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the הלכה is wrong. It is saying two תנאים who argue in the משנה cannot hold the exact same view, so the explanation of רבי מאיר needs to change.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to look for a different way to explain רבי מאיר, so that a real disagreement with רבי יהודה remains.

phrases.english: That is the view of Rabbi Yehuda!
For we learned in the Mishnah, Rabbi Yehuda says:
In the middle, he greets out of fear
and responds out of respect,
and at the breaks, he greets out of respect
and returns a greeting to any person?
phrases.notes: The question in the air is: if they say the same thing, what are they arguing about?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the combined result of steps 43 and 46
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבי מאיר's view built in steps 43 and 46
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These readings make רבי מאיר identical to רבי יהודה, which removes the disagreement the משנה presents.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: רבי מאיר's full view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is missing words. Read correctly, רבי מאיר holds that greeting and answering follow the same rule: respect at the breaks, and only fear in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet out of respect, and of course he may answer out of respect. In the middle of a paragraph, one may greet out of fear, and of course he may answer out of fear. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: To answer the last question, the גמרא says the משנה left some words out. It then reads רבי מאיר's view again with those words filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא read 'answering' as being more lenient than 'greeting', and that made רבי מאיר match רבי יהודה. Now 'needless to say he answers' means he answers under the SAME condition he may greet: out of respect at the breaks, and only out of fear in the middle. So for רבי מאיר, in the middle of a paragraph one may not answer someone you merely respect.
